metadata.attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2026; independent centerline digitization by OpenRacetrackDB
notes: The venue owner describes his complete paved four-kilometre road circuit in the Pikes Peak organizer interview. The circuit operator confirms 22 corners, three ravines and monthly lapping. The complete western main straight, northern technical sweep, eastern hooked hairpin and southern returns are independently visible on the pinned July 22, 2026 satellite raster. The northwestern access road, paddock loop, internal short connector and neighboring fields are excluded. Native satellite ground resolution is 10 m. Nearest-neighbor rendering does not add resolution. Fine corner alignment and historical direction remain draft; no vertices are fitted to private diagrams, timing positions or nominal distance. Independently digitized aerial centerline: 3764.7 m. Direction, historical configuration and fine corner alignment remain draft; no course coordinates come from the comparison catalogue.

sources.notes: Road surfaces are triangulated directly between this layout's saved border rings. Elevation follows the approximately 65 m terrain raster, not a survey of the road. Curbs are geometry-based illustrations on curved boundaries; their locations, widths, heights and colours are assumed, not extracted from imagery. Banking is unknown. The source trace and borders have too many unmatched cross-sections for safe lap reconstruction. Lap playback is unavailable. Boundary coordinates and their separate feature-level licence are preserved. Imagery loads externally on demand; no image bytes or meshes are stored.
